claims.quote: IPS >= 0.95 target

Also Test 5 line 921 blocks on a single dropped invariant, so the gate is really 1.0 when invariant counts are small (1 of 3 dropped = 0.67).

claims.quote: Altitude = a*AI + b*DI + (1 - g)*UI, a=.45, b=.40, g=.15
claims.evidence: Line 175 uses (1-gamma)=0.85 for UI; T4 code line 684-686 and operators/arcs_lte.py line 450 use 0.15. With 0.85, weights sum to 1.70, so raw_score*5 reaches 8.5 and saturates at L5 (any urgent text with AI=DI=0.1, UI=0.9 scores 4.25 = L4). The code silently fixed it; the spec formula is wrong.

Table says code-and-spec agree; they do not.
claims.fix: Generate the table from one source (the code constant) and cite it.

claims.quote: CF = 1 - (H(out)-H_inv)/(H(in)-H_inv)
claims.evidence: Divides by zero when the input is all invariants (H(in)=H_inv), goes negative for expansion (H(out) > H(in), the L0->L5 case at line 293), and CF=1 requires H(out)=H_inv, i.e. all non-invariant entropy removed. P3 line 53 requires '<= 5% semantic entropy loss', M6 line 786 requires CF >= 0.95 (>= 95% removed). Same word, opposite targets unless 'loss' means invariant loss. 'Shannon entropy of the semantic payload' has no estimator; code _estimate_entropy is a text statistic.
claims.fix: Define the estimator; restrict CF to compression; separate 'invariant loss' from 'style entropy removed'.

claims.quote: |psi_aud> = sum c_i |belief_i>, |c_i|^2 probability
claims.evidence: Requires sum|c_i|^2 = 1 and an orthonormal belief basis; neither is stated. Operators/arcs_lte.py lines 197, 210 store 'amplitudes' like [0.55,0.30,0.15] that sum to 1 as the values themselves, i.e. probabilities, not amplitudes (|c|^2 would be 0.30, 0.09, 0.02, sum 0.41). And _wavefunction_resonance (lines 490-520) never uses them: it is word overlap minus forbidden-word friction.
claims.fix: Specify construction of psi_msg and psi_aud (embedding? basis?) or label R a heuristic overlap score.

claims.quote: R = |<psi_msg|psi_aud>|^2 >= 0.80
claims.evidence: psi_msg is never defined, so R is not computable from the spec. Line 328: below 0.60 triggers Phase Warning and recompile; 0.60-0.80 behaviour undefined. Yellow Paper v1.2 section 2.1 (line 453-465) states the unsquared <psi_msg|psi_aud> ~ 1; the squared Born-rule form is the spec's own addition.
claims.fix: Define the representation and the 0.6-0.8 band.

claims.quote: destructive when phi1-phi2=pi; delta = |phi_msg - phi_aud| < 0.15
claims.evidence: Line 334 defines S1,S2 with different frequencies w1, w2; relative phase only governs interference at a common frequency (M8 line 800 uses a shared w). Phases of text are never defined, and R (a global-phase-invariant overlap) and delta are independent quantities, so R>=0.8 and delta<0.15 can disagree. |a-b| is not wrapped mod 2pi, so a pair at 0.1 and 2pi-0.05 reads 6.1 instead of 0.15. Code line 517 computes phase_delta = friction share * pi, not a phase.
claims.fix: Define phi operationally or drop delta as a separate gate; wrap to [0,pi].

claims.quote: BANDWAGON_AMPLIFY: Social proof injection (style op)

claims.evidence: T3.1 line 623 applies threshold 1.5 to np.gradient of abstraction scores bounded in [0,1]. Verified in Python: max |np.gradient| over a [0,1] signal is 1.0 (0.5 interior). The threshold can never fire. 1.5 is the Rx level-jump threshold (line 488) on a 0-5 scale: unit mismatch.

weak_joints: Altitude score formula (line 175 vs line 686): (1-gamma) makes weights sum 1.7; the 'empirically validated' weights have no data, and UI is not an altitude axis.
IPS gate: five different thresholds (0.95/0.90/0.85/1.0) and a keyword-overlap implementation whose recovery pass pastes invariants back in, so the 'non-negotiable' gate can be satisfied trivially.
Wavefunction/phase/geodesic math (M2, M4, M5, M8, T3): psi_msg, phase and the metric are undefined, so R and delta are not computable; the drift threshold 1.5 on a 0-1 signal can never fire.
